data.narrative:
Twenty, a Series A-stage Defense & Security company founded by Joe Lin, Leo Olson, Skyler Onken, and Pete Sorrentino, has raised $38M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 10 private and 2 public companies operating in the same sector, with primary focus on 3 same-stage private peers: Stark Defence ($4.0B), Singularity ($400M), and NODA AI ($125M).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $38M raised as a base proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, implies a valuation of $76M. Peer-median analysis across the three same-sector, same-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $400M, with a range spanning $125M to $4.0B. The wide peer range reflects significant heterogeneity within early-stage defense tech.

Synthesizing both methods produces a triangulated range of $65M (low) to $460M (high), with a median of $238M. The substantial gap between stage-progression and peer-median results reflects structural differences in how early-stage capital deployment and investor expectations vary across the defense ecosystem. Key uncertainties include Twenty's differentiation within the peer set, the relevance of outlier comparables (particularly Stark Defence at $4.0B), and whether raised capital adequately proxies for operational traction. Further diligence on revenue, unit economics, and customer concentration would refine this range.
